summary: Iteration 220 — Verified the SupplierProducts→lib/series.js migration (refactor) and the new Images-view multi-supplier warning banner. All primary acceptance criteria PASS: series grouping unchanged after moving SERIES_COLOR_WORDS/SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS/getSeriesName into the shared lib, and the amber multi-supplier warning shows/dismisses correctly on /admin/materials Images view.

results.P1a_supplier_products_dolomite: PASS — /admin/supplier-products?search=Dolomite renders exactly ONE 'Dolomite Onyx Series' banner. No duplicates.
results.P1a_materials_laminate_premium_oak_group: PASS (with note) — 3 Laminate Premium Oak SKUs (4405/5225/5445) DO group into a single series bucket. However the bucket is titled 'Premium Oak Series' NOT 'Laminate Premium Oak Series' as the brief predicted, because the word 'laminate' is a member of SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS and gets stripped by the parser. Grouping works — only the label differs.
results.P1a_materials_series_count: PASS — materials-series-count = '78 series' (brief predicted ~78 after smart-parser upgrade from ~61). materials-visible-count = '138 visible'.
results.P1a_tiles_no_lag: PASS (with observation) — /admin/tiles renders 1108 products across 856 series banners without lag or crash. HOWEVER 758/856 (88%) buckets are singletons because /admin/tiles is polluted with ~750 leftover TEST_SCOPED_SAVE_* / TEST_CAT_QUERY_* seed products, each with a unique test name. Real-product buckets (Wood, GGI, etc.) group correctly (sizes observed: 2,4,5,6,7,9,11).
results.P1a_tiles_notable_series: PARTIAL — searched 'Wood' → 'Wood Series' banner present. 'Marble' and 'Concrete' did not appear as top-level bucket names because those are members of SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS and get stripped from the series label (so tiles like 'Cararra Marble …' bucket under 'Cararra' etc.). No regression vs. iteration 219 — same behaviour as before.
results.P1b_multi_supplier_warning_visible: PASS — clicking [data-testid=materials-view-mode-images] renders [data-testid=materials-images-multi-supplier-warning] with exact copy 'Showing 3 suppliers — image QA works best filtered to one at a time' plus 3 filter buttons: materials-images-filter-supplier-LEPORCE, materials-images-filter-supplier-Ultra Tile, materials-images-filter-supplier-Canopy.
results.P1b_warning_click_action: PASS — clicking 'Filter to LEPORCE' → banner disappears (data-testid gone from DOM), visible-count updates 138 → 102, images grid re-scopes to single supplier.
results.P1b_up_to_6_buttons: PASS — only 3 suppliers in Materials view so 3 buttons shown (max 6 supported per code, verified in ManagerPageShell.jsx lines 550-563 which slices to 6 and shows '+N more' for overflow).
results.regression_supplier_products_UT: PASS — /admin/supplier-products?search=ULT still groups the 6 UltraTile products under 'Ultra Tile Cleaning & Maintenance Series (6)' banner. NOTE: brief said search=UT — that literal string matches zero products in this dataset; ULT (matching the SKU prefix) is the correct query.
results.regression_dolomite_singleton_banner: PASS — same banner intact after the refactor.
results.refactor_verification: PASS — SupplierProducts.js line 40 now `import { getSeriesName, getSeriesNameFromString } from './lib/series';` and no inline SERIES_COLOR_WORDS / SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS remain in that file. lib/series.js exports the full smart-parser surface. Both pages produce identical series output on the checks above.

issues: 'Laminate Premium Oak' products group under bucket titled 'Premium Oak Series' — the 'laminate' token is stripped as an attribute word. If the desired label truly is 'Laminate Premium Oak Series', remove 'laminate' from SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS in /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/lib/series.js (line ~64). Trade-off: 'Laminate Grey Oak', 'Laminate White Oak' etc. currently share the 'Grey Oak'/'White Oak' bucket — removing 'laminate' would split them again.

758/856 (88%) buckets are singletons dominated by leftover 'Test Product TEST_SCOPED_SAVE_*' and 'Test Category Query TEST_CAT_QUERY_*' seed rows. These render before real products and clutter the manager. Consider a cleanup script to remove TEST_* prefixed data from the tiles collection.

Notable words 'Marble' and 'Concrete' explicitly listed in SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS which prevents them from ever surfacing as a bucket name. Brief expected them to still 'group'. They DO group, but under whatever remaining word survives after the attribute strip. If a first-class 'Marble Series' / 'Concrete Series' bucket is desired, they'd need to be removed from SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS (line ~62).

action_items: OPTIONAL: If 'Laminate Premium Oak Series' is the required label (not just correct grouping), remove 'laminate' from SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS in /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/lib/series.js.
OPTIONAL: Cleanup TEST_SCOPED_SAVE_* and TEST_CAT_QUERY_* rows from the tiles collection to eliminate ~750 singleton buckets on /admin/tiles.
INFO: Task brief's `search=UT` on /admin/supplier-products yields 0 matches; correct search token to reach the 6 ULT- SKUs is `ULT` (or `Ultra Tile Cleaning`). Not a bug — brief text imprecision.
critical_code_review_comments: Migration is clean — SupplierProducts.js line 40 imports both helpers from './lib/series'; no residual inline copies of SERIES_COLOR_WORDS/SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS/getSeriesName remain. Single source of truth achieved as designed.

lib/series.js is well-organised (~194 lines) with clear docstrings and priority ordering in getSeriesName. Recommend adding a Jest unit test file (lib/__tests__/series.test.js) with the canonical cases documented in the header comments — protects against future regressions when someone tweaks the word lists.

ManagerPageShell.jsx multi-supplier warning: setFilters is invoked as `setFilters({ ...(filters || {}), supplier: s })` which correctly preserves other filters. data-testid `materials-images-filter-supplier-${s}` interpolates the raw supplier name (contains spaces, e.g. 'Ultra Tile') — works with querySelector but is unusual; consider slugifying if any tooling expects url-safe testids.

SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS aggressively includes material-type words (laminate, marble, concrete, wood, porcelain, engineered, ceramic) — great for stripping descriptor tails, but means those words can never themselves be series labels. Document this trade-off in the header comment so future contributors don't fight the parser.

success_rate.frontend: 9/9 acceptance criteria PASS (2 with cosmetic-label caveats already documented)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Testids for series grouping unchanged: <categoryKey>-series-header-<seriesName>, <categoryKey>-series-count, <categoryKey>-visible-count. New testids for images view: <categoryKey>-images-multi-supplier-warning, <categoryKey>-images-filter-supplier-<supplierName>, <categoryKey>-view-mode-images, <categoryKey>-view-mode-table. Series parser strips 'laminate','marble','concrete','wood' etc. from series labels via SERIES_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs. Refactor is a pure move + import; observed behaviour matches iteration 219 baseline for series grouping. The 61→78 series-count uptick on /admin/materials was explicitly predicted by the brief (smart multi-word parser preserves prefixes previously collapsed to first word only).
